#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release draft lifecycle guard (issue #282): a run that creates a release
# draft must end with it published or deleted — never orphan it. `gh
# release create <tag> <assets...>` uploads the assets through a DRAFT
# first and publishes only after every upload succeeds; a step dying
# mid-upload (the v0.1.190 rot) leaves that draft behind forever.
#
# Usage: release_draft_guard.sh <tag>
#
# OWNERSHIP-SCOPED DELETE (review of #294): the guard deletes ONLY the
# draft this very run+job created. daily-publish runs the macOS and
# mobile legs concurrently against the same derived tag; a failed leg's
# guard firing on the SIBLING leg's mid-upload draft would destroy a
# healthy concurrent release. Draft-capable creates
# (scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh, scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh)
# stamp the draft body with
#   <!-- release-draft-owner: run/<run_id>/job/<job_id> -->
# and the guard deletes only on an exact match against GITHUB_RUN_ID /
# GITHUB_JOB (both GitHub Actions default env). Matrix jobs share
# GITHUB_JOB across legs (ci.yml binaries, build-macos.yml
# build-macos-cli) — those steps stamp a LEG-SUFFIXED identity via
# RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (e.g. run/123/job/binaries-linux-x64) and the
# guard step must export the same value, so a failed leg can never match
# a sibling's in-flight draft. A foreign or unmarked draft is NEVER
# deleted here — the daily sweeper
# (scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh) reclaims genuinely orphaned drafts
# after 24h.
#
# Called from workflow steps with `if: always() && job.status != 'success'`
# so it runs on failure AND cancellation. A published release or a missing
# release is a no-op; a draft for <tag> is deleted (its assets are
# unpublished by definition — published releases are the artifact store,
# issue #282 E2). The tag itself is never touched.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_draft_guard.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
: "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}"
: "${GITHUB_JOB:?GITHUB_JOB must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}"
identity="${RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY:-run/$GITHUB_RUN_ID/job/$GITHUB_JOB}"
# Validate (mirror of release_lazy_draft.sh): an unmatchable identity
# would silently orphan the draft forever.
printf '%s' "$identity" | grep -Eq '^run/[0-9]+/job/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$' || {
  echo "::error::RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY '$identity' does not match 'run/<id>/job/<name>' — the marker could never be stamped or matched" >&2
  exit 1
}

state=$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json isDraft --jq .isDraft 2>/dev/null || echo missing)
if [ "$state" != "true" ]; then
  echo "release lifecycle guard: $tag is ${state} (published or absent) — nothing to clean"
  exit 0
fi

# Factory · AI Teammate leg — REUSABLE workflow (dmtools-agents factory pack, top-level: GitHub requires reusable workflows at the .github/workflows root — no subdirectories).
#
# The dev→review→rework machine loop for GitHub-issues trackers, hosted in
# dmtools-agents so target repositories carry only a thin stub (event
# triggers + this call) plus .dmtools/config.js, secrets and vars. Runs in
# the CALLER's context: github.repository = the target repo; vars.* and
# secrets.* resolve from the caller (each target pins its own versions).
#
# Legs (guard derives the slot when `leg` is empty):
#   bug | story | review | rework — the runner configs live in the TARGET repo
#   (.dmtools/runners/*), wired via .dmtools/config.js sm.runners.
#
# Loop mechanics (identical to the dmtools-dart template this was ported
# from — see that file's history for the full rationale):
#   issue assigned/labeled → guard → ticket input → dmtools run <runner>
#   → agent develops → PR ("Closes #NN") → review verdict step:
#       APPROVE + green PR checks → pr_approved → merge (merge-trigger/stub)
#       CHANGES_REQUESTED        → agent:rework (bounded: MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS,
#                                  then needs-human escalation)
#   Review/rework queue labels are stripped at cycle end (no self-loops).
#   fa sessions ride the fa-sess/gh-<n> branch (cache saves are denied on
#   issues-event runs); fa project memory is committed back to the repo.
#
# Secrets (via `secrets: inherit`): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (PAT — labels added
#   with GITHUB_TOKEN never fire `labeled` events; pushes must not author
#   as github-actions[bot]), ZAI_CODE_KEY, KIMI_REVIEW_KEY.
# Vars: FA_VERSION_MACHINE || FA_VERSION || latest, DMTOOLS_VERSION,
#   MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS (default 2).
#
# Caller stub:
#   on:
#     issues: {types: [assigned, labeled]}
#     workflow_dispatch: {inputs: {issue: {type: number}, leg: {type: string}}}
#   concurrency:
#     group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue }}
#     cancel-in-progress: false
#   jobs:
#     factory:
#       uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@<ref>
#       with:
#         issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue }}
#         leg: ${{ inputs.leg || '' }}
#         reason: ${{ inputs.reason || 'stub' }}

name: 'Factory · AI Teammate'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      # The ref THIS awf repo was invoked at — a reusable workflow runs in
      # the CALLER's context, so github.workflow_ref carries the caller's ref
      # (dart's branch), which is meaningless against the awf remote. The
      # stub passes its own pin here (main in production) — same pattern as
      factory_home_ref:
        description: Awf ref the caller pinned factory-teammate.yml to
        type: string
        required: false
        default: main
      runner:
        description: 'Runner label (self-hosted pools must be visible to the CALLING org)'
        type: string
        default: 'ubuntu-slim'
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (string: number-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions). Empty when pr is given (PR-anchored run, #687).'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687). Exactly one of issue|pr must be set.'
        required: false
        type: string
      checkout_ref:
        description: 'IstiN/dmtools-agents#1096 (gh-1075 fork-PR dispatch): refs/pull/<N>/head to check out instead of the dispatch ref, so a fork leg works the PR head tree. Empty = default checkout (byte-identical).'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      machine-author:
        description: "Deployment's machine (bot) login (#687): gates rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews (auto-approve via pr_approved is author-agnostic per the owner rule). Injected as jobParams.machineAuthor — branch-independent (the checked-out PR branch carries no machineAuthor config)."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: "Which leg to run: dev | review | rework (empty = derive from labels/assignees)"
        required: false
        type: string
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      # Optional agent-work toolchains (salvaged from #35): "" (default)
      # installs NOTHING — explicit opt-in per caller. The dmtools engine
      # and its dart runtime are installed by install-dmtools-cli.sh and
      # are NEVER gated on these inputs.
      java-version:
        description: 'JDK for agent work (Temurin, Gradle/Maven cache). "" (default) installs NOTHING. e.g. "21".'
        required: false
        default: ''
        type: string
      node-version:
        description: 'Node.js for agent work (npm cache). "" (default) installs NOTHING. e.g. "20".'
        required: false
        default: ''
        type: string
      python-version:
        description: 'Python for agent work. "" (default) installs NOTHING. e.g. "3.12".'
        required: false
        default: ''
        type: string
      flutter-version:
        description: 'Flutter SDK for agent work (cached). "" (default) installs NOTHING — most consumers are not Flutter projects and bring their own toolchain via the setup/install scripts. A value installs Flutter+matching Dart via flutter-action with SDK caching (e.g. "stable", "3.38.0"); Flutter targets (fa) pass it explicitly.'
        required: false
        default: ''
        type: string
      dart-version:
        description: 'Dart SDK for agent work via dart-lang/setup-dart@v1 (~7s, vs ~90s for Flutter SDK). "" (default) installs NOTHING. e.g. "stable", "3.9.0". Pure-Dart targets (dmtools-dart) pass this instead of flutter-version.'
        required: false
        default: ''
        type: string

      CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY1_NAME:
        description: 'Env var name for slot 1 (plain input, not secret).'
        required: false
        type: string
      CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY2_NAME:
        description: 'Env var name for slot 2 (plain input, not secret).'
        required: false
        type: string
      CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY3_NAME:
        description: 'Env var name for slot 3 (plain input, not secret).'
        required: false
        type: string

    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN:
        description: 'PAT with repo scope — machine labels, pushes, PR/issue API (secrets: inherit does not cross repository boundaries).'
        required: true
      ZAI_CODE_KEY:
        description: 'z.ai API key (dev/rework provider + review queue fallback)'
        required: false
      KIMI_REVIEW_KEY:
        description: 'kimi API key (review provider, first in the queue)'
        required: false
      ZAI_CODE_KEY_1:
        description: 'z.ai fallback key slot 1 (separate account) - lands in the job env as ZAI_CODE_KEY_1 for the fa provider resolver (gh-1381)'
        required: false
      ZAI_CODE_KEY_2:
        description: 'z.ai fallback key slot 2 - see ZAI_CODE_KEY_1.'
        required: false
      ZAI_CODE_KEY_3:
        description: 'z.ai fallback key slot 3 - see ZAI_CODE_KEY_1.'
        required: false
      ZAI_CODE_KEY_4:
        description: 'z.ai fallback key slot 4 - see ZAI_CODE_KEY_1.'
        required: false
      ZAI_CODE_KEY_5:
        description: 'z.ai fallback key slot 5 - see ZAI_CODE_KEY_1.'
        required: false
      CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY1:
        description: 'Generic provider-key slot 1 — value lands in the agent job env under CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY1_NAME. The factory never knows key names; the caller stub documents which repo secret maps here.'
        required: false
      CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY2:
        description: 'Generic provider-key slot 2 — see CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY1.'
        required: false
      CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY3:
        description: 'Generic provider-key slot 3 — see CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY1.'
        required: false
      APP_ID:
        description: 'Optional GitHub App id (awf#52). With APP_PRIVATE_KEY set, every GitHub API call and git push in the leg rides a per-job App installation token (10x the PAT rate budget — the ai-teammate PAT exhausted its 5000 req/h and killed SM ticks, dmtools-agents run 39034080472) instead of SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN. Absent => PAT, byte-identical to the pre-App behavior.'
        required: false
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY:
        description: 'Private key (PEM) of the APP_ID GitHub App.'
        required: false
      ENV_VAR_DEV_QUEUE:
        description: 'FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE JSON for dev/rework runners (fa-bug-dev, fa-story-dev, fa-rework); may also be passed via vars.ENV_VAR_DEV_QUEUE.'
        required: false
      ENV_VAR_REVIEW_QUEUE:
        description: 'FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE JSON for review runner (fa-review); may also be passed via vars.ENV_VAR_REVIEW_QUEUE.'
        required: false

# NOTE: no `concurrency` here — the caller stub owns the per-issue group.
# A reusable workflow with the SAME group as its caller deadlocks: the caller
# holds the group while the called workflow waits for it forever (pending, 0 jobs).

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  # actions/cache@v6 save phase needs actions:write on github.token.
  actions: write

jobs:
  guard:
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner || 'ubuntu-slim' }}
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run }}
      runner: ${{ steps.check.outputs.runner }}
      config: ${{ steps.check.outputs.config }}
      kind: ${{ steps.check.outputs.kind }}
      anchor: ${{ steps.check.outputs.anchor }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout target repository (config, runners)
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # caller-repo checkout: the factory reads .dmtools/config.js from
          # the TARGET repository, never from the factory pack
          ref: ${{ github.ref }}
          # gate job only: config.js at the head + API guards — no git
          # history walks. fetch-depth 0 cloned the FULL history here
          # (~1 min on fa, every leg) for nothing.
          fetch-depth: 1

      # GitHub App auth (awf#52): with APP_ID + APP_PRIVATE_KEY secrets,
      # every GitHub API call / git push in this job rides a per-job App
      # installation token instead of the PAT. Minted HERE, in each
      # consuming job, because GitHub strips secret-bearing job outputs
      # (tokens cannot cross jobs). Absent APP_* secrets =>
      # SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN / github.token exactly as before.
      - name: Resolve GitHub auth (App -> PAT)
        id: app
        env:
          APP_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$APP_ID" ]; then
            echo "enabled=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "auth: app"
          else
            echo "enabled=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "auth: pat"
          fi

      - name: Mint GitHub App installation token
        id: app-token
        if: steps.app.outputs.enabled == 'true'
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v2
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      - name: Set up Java for agent work
        if: inputs.java-version != ''
        uses: actions/setup-java@v5
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: ${{ inputs.java-version }}
          cache: gradle
      - name: Set up Node.js for agent work
        if: inputs.node-version != ''
        uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: ${{ inputs.node-version }}
      - name: Set up Python for agent work
        if: inputs.python-version != ''
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ inputs.python-version }}
      - name: Fetch factory scripts (this repo @ invocation ref)
        # Stage-2 de-bloat delivery: the guard's domain step (scripts/
        # teammate-dispatch-gate.sh) rides the same immutable factory-kit
        # fetch as the teammate job — scripts/ is checked out at EXACTLY the
        # ref the caller invoked (github.workflow_ref), so the gate logic can
        # never skew from the workflow version that calls it. Strict, unlike
        # the teammate fetch: the guard has no FACTORY_ROOT fallback, so a
        # failed delivery must red the run, not silently skip the gate.
        env:
          AWF_REF: ${{ inputs.factory_home_ref }}
        run: |
          ref="$AWF_REF"
          dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit"
          git init -q "$dir"
          git -C "$dir" remote add origin https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows.git
          git -C "$dir" fetch -q --depth 1 origin "$ref" \
            || { echo "::error::factory scripts fetch failed at $ref — the dispatch gate cannot run"; exit 1; }
          git -C "$dir" checkout -q FETCH_HEAD -- scripts/
          [ -f "$dir/scripts/teammate-dispatch-gate.sh" ] \
            || { echo "::error::scripts/teammate-dispatch-gate.sh missing at $ref"; exit 1; }
      - name: Decide whether this event is for the agent
        id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ inputs.issue }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ inputs.pr }}
          # Event context rides through from the caller (issues events) —
          # empty for pure dispatches. The guard ALWAYS refreshes from the
          # API (queued runs see a stale payload); this is only a fallback.
          ASSIGNEES: ${{ join(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, ' ') }}
          LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, ' ') }}
          ACTOR: ${{ github.event.action || github.event_name }}
          # #544: the `labeled` event sender — the owner-override gate checks
          # its repo permission before honoring a manual agent:rework.
          # Empty for schedule-scan dispatches (SM ticks): the label is
          # trusted as-is there (see rework_override_ok below).
          SENDER: ${{ github.event.sender.login || '' }}
          # Comment-resume: issue_comment events re-arm a dev leg when
          # the first HUMAN reply lands on an ai_questions_asked ticket.
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          COMMENT_AUTHOR: ${{ github.event.comment.user.login || '' }}
          COMMENT_ID: ${{ github.event.comment.id || '' }}
          INPUT_LEG: ${{ inputs.leg }}
          INPUT_REASON: ${{ inputs.reason }}
          # The assignee gate below compares against the machine login.
          # AGENT_HANDLE lives on the TEAMMATE job's env — without it here
          # the guard's $AGENT_HANDLE is empty, `grep -w` never matches, and
          # assignment-triggered dev legs never start (live: dmtools-dart
          # run 35519287617 — issue #173 assigned to ai-teammate → skipped).
          AGENT_HANDLE: ai-teammate
        # Body: scripts/teammate-dispatch-gate.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/teammate-dispatch-gate.sh"

  teammate:
    needs: guard
    if: needs.guard.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner || 'ubuntu-slim' }}
    # A real fix is a 40-80 minute agent session (gh-623 burned a full RCA +
    # TDD cycle at exactly 61 minutes and the job was killed mid-work); dev
    # legs over Flutter sources run the analyzer + full flutter test suite
    # and live 2-3 hours (fa gh-1077 leg was killed mid-work at exactly 110
    # on 2026-09-30). The autocommit timer (300s) bounds the blast radius of
    # a kill; this timeout bounds the bill.
    timeout-minutes: 260
    # Workflow-level env is NOT supported in reusable (workflow_call)
    # workflows — the factory failed validation at startup until this
    # moved down to the job.
    env:
      AGENT_HANDLE: ai-teammate
      FA_VERSION: ${{ vars.FA_VERSION_MACHINE || vars.FA_VERSION || 'latest' }}
      DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'latest' }}
      MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS: ${{ vars.MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS || 2 }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout target repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # dmtools-agents#1096: fork-PR legs check out refs/pull/<N>/head;
          # empty resolves the default ref exactly as before.
          ref: ${{ inputs.checkout_ref || '' }}
          # NO submodules and NO agents fetch here: the factory works with
          # RELEASES (factory kit + per-agent packs), it never materializes
          # the dmtools-agents tree in leg worktrees — that tree is the
          # integration-TEST target's own business (epam/dmtools-dart#412
          # fetches dmtools-agents@main in its own quality.yml).
          # Materializing agents/ here produced embedded-repo gitlinks
          # (dart ai/gh-379, fa ai/gh-1646/1643, 2026-10-16).
          persist-credentials: false


      # GitHub App auth (awf#52): with APP_ID + APP_PRIVATE_KEY secrets,
      # every GitHub API call / git push in this job rides a per-job App
      # installation token instead of the PAT. Minted HERE, in each
      # consuming job, because GitHub strips secret-bearing job outputs
      # (tokens cannot cross jobs). Absent APP_* secrets =>
      # SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN / github.token exactly as before.
      - name: Resolve GitHub auth (App -> PAT)
        id: app
        env:
          APP_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$APP_ID" ]; then
            echo "enabled=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "auth: app"
          else
            echo "enabled=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "auth: pat"
          fi

      - name: Mint GitHub App installation token
        id: app-token
        if: steps.app.outputs.enabled == 'true'
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v2
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      - name: "Fetch factory kit (this repo @ invocation ref — immutable)"
        # Trust-boundary scripts (git push guard, source PAT credentials)
        # ride the SAME immutable ref the caller invoked this workflow at
        # (github.workflow_ref = owner/repo/.github/workflows/<name>.yml@<ref>)
        # — a PR head can no longer supply them (self-host security,
        # 2026-10-01) and the script version can never skew from the workflow
        # version that calls it. Plain git (no action): GitLab-portable.
        #
        # RUNNER_TEMP, never $GITHUB_WORKSPACE: a nested git repo inside the
        # workspace poisons every downstream `git add` (the gitlink "does
        # not have a commit checked out", exit 128 — live fa gh-1000
        # 2026-10-03: PR staging, origin-sync clean-tree gate, and the
        # session timer auto-commit all tripped on it).
        env:
          AWF_REF: ${{ inputs.factory_home_ref }}
        run: |
          ref="$AWF_REF"
          dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit"
          git init -q "$dir"
          git -C "$dir" remote add origin https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows.git
          git -C "$dir" fetch -q --depth 1 origin "$ref" \
            || { echo "::warning::kit fetch failed — falling back to FACTORY_ROOT copies"; exit 0; }
          git -C "$dir" checkout -q FETCH_HEAD -- kit/
          git -C "$dir" checkout -q FETCH_HEAD -- scripts/ 2>/dev/null || true  # stage-1 de-bloat: step bodies live in scripts/ (same immutable ref)
          [ -f "$dir/kit/git-push-guard.sh" ] || { echo "::warning::kit incomplete at $ref — falling back"; rm -rf "$dir"; exit 0; }
          # Kit liveness probe (awf#7): a guard whose shebang is not line 1
          # silently executes under /bin/sh and dies with "Syntax error" on
          # every git call — the whole dev session loses git (branch setup,
          # timer auto-commit, PR post-action) with quiet skips downstream.
          head -1 "$dir/kit/git-push-guard.sh" | grep -q '^#!.*bash' \
            || { echo "::error::kit git-push-guard.sh lost its shebang (line 1) at $ref — refusing to arm a broken guard"; exit 1; }
          cp "$dir/kit/git-push-guard.sh" "$RUNNER_TEMP/git-probe" && chmod +x "$RUNNER_TEMP/git-probe"
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/git-probe" version >/dev/null 2>&1 \
            || { echo "::error::kit git-push-guard.sh does not execute (probe failed) at $ref"; exit 1; }

      - name: "Fetch factory-setup (dmtools-agents releases — no tree checkout)"
        # Owner mandate 2026-10-03: the factory NEVER clones the
        # dmtools-agents tree. The workflow glue the run needs —
        # setup/ toolbelt (install.sh, cache.sh, review-verdict.sh,
        # fa-session.sh, ...), scripts/git-push-guard.sh fallback and the
        # four legacy leg configs — ships as the factory-setup-*.zip
        # release asset (built by ci/release_packs.mjs, rides every
        # agents-rel-* tag).
        # Compat: a pre-mounted factory-agents/ tree still WINS over the
        # zip — hosts that intentionally mount the tree (dmtools-agents'
        # own factory-probe, forks pinning local trees) keep their copies.
        # FACTORY_ROOT carries the winner for every later step.
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}
          PACK_TAG: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY }}
          # awf#25: AGENTS_VERSION is the documented pin knob (same
          # semantics as factory-sm.yml) — when pinned to a concrete
          # agents-rel-* tag it takes PRECEDENCE over the registry
          # variable for the setup pack AND the runtime pack registry.
          AGENTS_KNOB: ${{ vars.AGENTS_VERSION || 'latest' }}
        # Body: scripts/fetch-factory-setup.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/fetch-factory-setup.sh"

      - name: "Resolve parent config (pack launch.json wins, tree fallback)"
        # Wave 2 (owner 2026-10-01): teammate packs are self-sufficient —
        # the unpacked pack's launch.json IS the launch contract and WINS
        # over the legacy tree copy. Pack cache root (dmtools
        # AgentPackResolver): ~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<version>/ —
        # populated by `dmtools run` resolving a <agent>@latest parent, so
        # it is visible here on persistent-HOME/self-hosted runners and to
        # every step AFTER the agent run; fresh hosted runners fall back to
        # the legacy tree config until the run unpacks the pack. Neither
        # source present ⇒ loud fail (old pin without tree configs and
        # without a Wave-2 pack). fa-session.sh/run-agent.sh derive the
        # agent identity from the pack DIR, so naming stays stable either
        # way. Plain bash: GitLab-portable.
        env:
          LEGACY_CONFIG: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.config }}
        # Body: scripts/resolve-parent-config.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/resolve-parent-config.sh"

      - name: Export fa session identity + cache keys
        # AI_TEAMMATE_CONFIG_FILE comes from the resolve step above
        # (pack launch.json wins) via GITHUB_ENV.
        env:
          AI_TEAMMATE_DISPLAY_KEY: GH-${{ needs.guard.outputs.anchor }}
          AI_TEAMMATE_CONCURRENCY_KEY: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.anchor }}
        run: bash "${FACTORY_ROOT}/setup/cache.sh" keys fa-session

      - name: Restore fa session (resume the ticket conversation)
        # actions/cache saves are denied on issues-event runs (job token is
        # cache-read-only there), so the session tree rides a dedicated git
        # branch per issue; the per-issue concurrency group serializes writers.
        env:
          FA_SESS_BRANCH: fa-sess/${{ needs.guard.outputs.anchor }}
        # Engine-side since dmtools-agents#943: the fa-session restore from the
        # fa-sess/<anchor> git branch is session-lifecycle logic and ships in
        # the factory-setup zip (pack agents-rel-20261016-215704+). The awf
        # copy is gone — this is the only source now (ordered flip: pack
        # landed first).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-setup/scripts/restore-fa-session.sh"

      - name: Cache fa CLI (by version)
        if: env.FA_VERSION != 'latest'
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.local/bin/fa
            ~/lib
          key: fa-${{ env.FA_VERSION }}-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' (or empty) resolves to the current release tag so the
        # version-locked install.sh URL keeps working; owner mandate
        # 2026-10-01: machine legs always track the latest CLI/agents.
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}
        # Body: scripts/resolve-dmtools-version.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/resolve-dmtools-version.sh"

      - name: Cache dmtools CLI (by version)
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: ~/.dmtools/bin
          key: dmtools-${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION }}-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}

      - name: "Install prerequisites (fa; no-op on cache hit)"
        # Authenticated gh api download first — anonymous release-asset
        # downloads hit GitHub edge caches that served stale 404s for hours
        # after a re-cut release (observed 2026-09-12).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}
        # Body: scripts/install-fa-cli.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/install-fa-cli.sh"

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        # The installer ships as a release asset, version-locked to the
        # bundle it installs — no copy of install.sh in the target repo.
        # Body: scripts/install-dmtools-cli.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/install-dmtools-cli.sh"

      # flutter-action treats a literal version string strictly — the words
      # stable/beta/main/master are CHANNELS and crash the action ("Unable
      # to determine Flutter version for channel: stable", live: gh-623 run
      # 35370007049). Two steps with plain if-comparisons — the GH parser
      # rejects map-indexing expressions inside with:.
      - name: Set up Flutter for agent work (channel)
        if: inputs.flutter-version == 'stable' || inputs.flutter-version == 'beta' || inputs.flutter-version == 'main' || inputs.flutter-version == 'master'
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with:
          channel: ${{ inputs.flutter-version }}
          cache: true

      - name: Set up Flutter for agent work (pinned version)
        if: inputs.flutter-version != '' && !(inputs.flutter-version == 'stable' || inputs.flutter-version == 'beta' || inputs.flutter-version == 'main' || inputs.flutter-version == 'master')
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with:
          flutter-version: ${{ inputs.flutter-version }}
          cache: true

      - name: Set up Dart for agent work
        if: inputs.dart-version != '' && inputs.flutter-version == ''
        uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: ${{ inputs.dart-version }}

      - name: Verify prerequisites
        env:
          FLUTTER_VERSION: ${{ inputs.flutter-version }}
          DART_VERSION: ${{ inputs.dart-version }}
        # Body: scripts/verify-prerequisites.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/verify-prerequisites.sh"

      - name: Configure Git Author + push credentials
        # Purge the checkout's App token and make SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN the
        # credential that wins for github.com pushes (all logic in the
        # shared installer — one copy serves every push path in the job).
        env:
          SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/kit/install-source-git-credentials.sh" 2>/dev/null \
            || bash "${FACTORY_ROOT}/setup/install-source-git-credentials.sh"

      - name: Trace git credential stack (push-time evidence)
        # gh-63 Task 1 — same run that pushes, right before the agent.
        # What each section proves:
        #   --show-origin        WHERE each credential source lives; the
        #                        extraheader section must come back empty —
        #                        asserted below, so any resurrection of the
        #                        App-token header (checkout layout change,
        #                        mid-run config write) fails the run here
        #                        instead of silently re-arming bot pushes
        #   submodule foreach    same proof for each submodule local config
        #                        (checkout arms those with submodules: true)
        #   git credential fill  dry-runs the exact push-path resolution and
        #                        shows the winning username; the password is
        #                        masked, and the helper's stderr line confirms
        #                        SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN served the credential
        env:
          SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        # Body: scripts/trace-git-credentials.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/trace-git-credentials.sh"

      - name: Seed local git excludes (factory workspace artifacts)
        # Everything the factory/agent scribbles into the workspace that must
        # NEVER reach a commit (agents run `git add -A`). .git/info/exclude is
        # local-only by construction — no .gitignore pollution in agent PRs.
        # Body: scripts/seed-git-excludes.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/seed-git-excludes.sh"

      - name: Write the issue into the agent input folder
        if: inputs.pr == ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ inputs.issue }}
        # Body: scripts/write-input-issue.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/write-input-issue.sh"

      - name: Write the PR into the agent input folder (PR-anchored runs)
        # #687: the PR is the anchor — the pr-N contextId is what the agent
        # scripts key on; ticket.json carries the same tracker-contract
        # shape so hydration paths stay uniform.
        if: inputs.pr != ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ inputs.pr }}
        # Body: scripts/write-input-pr.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/write-input-pr.sh"

      - name: Mark machine job started (issue task list)
        # Deterministic start marker in the issue body — survives agent
        # crashes/timeouts because the DONE twin below runs on always().
        # Contract: a "## Machine jobs" section with one task-list line per
        # factory run; the line's run URL is the unique id used to flip it.
        # PR-anchored runs skip it: no issue body to carry the task list.
        if: inputs.pr == ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ inputs.issue }}
          JOB_LEG: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.kind }}
          RUNNER: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.runner }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        # Body: scripts/mark-job-started.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/mark-job-started.sh"

      - name: Export custom provider key slots (1-3) → job env
        # Generic numbered slots (owner decision 2026-10-13): the factory
        # never hardcodes provider key names — the caller stub maps each
        # slot from a plain repo secret and names the env var it lands as
        # (the stub comment documents the slot→key mapping). Values ride
        # the secrets context → runner-masked natively in every log; empty
        # slots are skipped, half-configured slots warn.
        env:
          CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY1: ${{ secrets.CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY1 }}
          CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY1_NAME: ${{ inputs.CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY1_NAME }}
          CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY2: ${{ secrets.CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY2 }}
          CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY2_NAME: ${{ inputs.CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY2_NAME }}
          CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY3: ${{ secrets.CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY3 }}
          CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY3_NAME: ${{ inputs.CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY3_NAME }}
        # Body: scripts/export-provider-key-slots.sh (stage-1 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/export-provider-key-slots.sh"

      - name: Run agent (fa provider via runner env overrides)
        id: run_agent
        # Hard cap under the job's 260 min: a hung agent session must FAIL
        # the leg (the always() post-actions then run inside the remaining
        # budget and the red path re-queues) instead of the job-level
        # timeout killing everything mid-post-action. NOT 45: a real fix is
        # a 40-80 minute session (gh-623 was killed mid-work at exactly 61).
        # NOT 110: dev legs over Flutter sources run the analyzer + the
        # full flutter test suite — fa gh-1077 was killed mid-work at
        # exactly 110 (live flutter_tester orphans at teardown, PR step
        # never reached) — 2026-09-30.
        timeout-minutes: 240
        env:
          CI_RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          RUNNER: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.runner }}
          AI_AGENT_PROVIDER: fa
          # dmtools-agents#1096: the rework leg reads the fork pull ref
          # (js/common/forkCheckout.js envCheckoutRef) — empty for same-repo.
          CHECKOUT_REF: ${{ inputs.checkout_ref }}
          # AI_TEAMMATE_CONFIG_FILE rides GITHUB_ENV from the resolve step
          # (pack launch.json wins, legacy tree fallback).
          AI_TEAMMATE_DISPLAY_KEY: GH-${{ needs.guard.outputs.anchor }}
          AI_TEAMMATE_CONCURRENCY_KEY: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.anchor }}
          ZAI_CODE_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY }}
          # gh-1381 fallback keys: literal pass-through — absent secrets resolve to
          # empty strings, which the fa provider resolver treats as "no fallback"
          # (it probes ZAI_CODE_KEY_1.._5 for same-provider failover entries).
          ZAI_CODE_KEY_1: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY_1 }}
          ZAI_CODE_KEY_2: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY_2 }}
          ZAI_CODE_KEY_3: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY_3 }}
          ZAI_CODE_KEY_4: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY_4 }}
          ZAI_CODE_KEY_5: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY_5 }}
          KIMI_REVIEW_KEY: ${{ secrets.KIMI_REVIEW_KEY }}
          ENV_VAR_DEV_QUEUE: ${{ secrets.ENV_VAR_DEV_QUEUE || vars.ENV_VAR_DEV_QUEUE }}
          ENV_VAR_REVIEW_QUEUE: ${{ secrets.ENV_VAR_REVIEW_QUEUE || vars.ENV_VAR_REVIEW_QUEUE }}
          SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # Agent-pack registry base (dm.ai #579): runners may parent packs
          # by REGISTRY ref (`pr_review@latest`) — the resolver reads the
          # releases base (incl. catalog.json) from this env. Callers set
          # the repo VARIABLE to their pinned dmtools-agents release tag;
          # unset (or empty) keeps the previous file-only behavior and the
          # resolver fails with an explicit "no pack registry" error.
          DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY }}
          # gh operations inside the session must act AS the SOURCE account:
          # events created with GITHUB_TOKEN do not trigger workflows.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || github.token }}
        run: |
          # awf#25 pin parity: when the setup resolved a concrete
          # agents-rel-* tag, the runtime registry base must point at
          # THAT release (catalog + zips + .sha256 sidecars), not the
          # floating repo variable — otherwise `<agent>@latest` refs
          # bypass the pin and a broken newest release takes down pinned
          # fleets (live: fa pr-1350 review leg 2026-10-06). Mirrors
          # factory-sm.yml's tick export and merge-trigger's derive.
          if [ -n "${RESOLVED_AGENTS_TAG:-}" ]; then
            export DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY="https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/releases/download/${RESOLVED_AGENTS_TAG}"
            echo "→ pack registry pinned to ${RESOLVED_AGENTS_TAG} (AGENTS_VERSION parity, awf#25)"
          fi
          # #542 mechanical guard: interpose the git push/commit guard shim at
          # the FRONT of PATH before `dmtools run` so EVERY push path in the
          # session is covered — both the fa agent's own shell tool (inherits
          # the dmtools process env) and the JS pre/post-actions'
          # cli_execute_command (PATH-resolved `git`). Refuses pushes to
          # main/master/default branch and closing keywords in commit
          # messages. Deliberately NOT written to $GITHUB_PATH: later workflow
          # steps (session-branch persistence) push legitimately.
          GIT_GUARD_BIN="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/git-push-guard-bin"
          mkdir -p "${GIT_GUARD_BIN}"
          GUARD="${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/kit/git-push-guard.sh"
          [ -f "$GUARD" ] || GUARD="${FACTORY_ROOT}/scripts/git-push-guard.sh"
          ln -sf "$GUARD" "${GIT_GUARD_BIN}/git"
          export PATH="${GIT_GUARD_BIN}:${PATH}"
          git --version  # resolves through the shim — proves the wiring
          # FULL session trace: FA_LOG_FILE tees every line fa prints to the
          # file, uploaded as an artifact below; dmtools mirrors child output
          # live to its own stderr, so the agent's work streams into the log.
          FA_LOG_FILE="${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/.dmtools/fa-trace.log"
          export FA_LOG_FILE
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "${FA_LOG_FILE}")"
          touch "${FA_LOG_FILE}"
          echo "fa full trace: ${FA_LOG_FILE}"
          # Body: scripts/dmtools-selfheal.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
          # SOURCED so the healed PATH propagates to the rest of the step).
          . "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/dmtools-selfheal.sh"
          RUN_OUTPUT="${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/.dmtools/run-output.txt"
          # #687: machine login rides jobParams so PR-anchored verdicts arm
          # the merge pipeline regardless of what the checked-out branch's
          # .dmtools/config.js carries (postPRReviewComments reads
          # jobParams.machineAuthor first).
          DMTOOLS_ARGS=()
          MA='${{ inputs.machine-author }}'
          if [ -n "$MA" ]; then
            DMTOOLS_ARGS+=('{"params":{"jobParams":{"machineAuthor":"'"$MA"'"}}}')
          fi
          # Engine-side since dmtools-agents#943: the fa-trace watchdog ships
          # in the factory-setup zip (pack agents-rel-20261016-215704+); the
          # awf copy is gone — this is the only source now (ordered flip:
          # pack landed first). Backgrounded like the inline `( ... ) &`
          # subshell it replaced at extraction.
          RUN_OUTPUT="${RUN_OUTPUT}" bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-setup/scripts/fa-trace-watchdog.sh" &
          WATCHDOG_PID=$!
          # Body: scripts/stall-capture.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
          # backgrounded like the inline `( ... ) &` subshell it replaces).
          bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/stall-capture.sh" &
          STALL_MON_PID=$!
          trap 'kill "${WATCHDOG_PID}" "${STALL_MON_PID}" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
          dmtools run "${RUNNER}" ${DMTOOLS_ARGS[@]+"${DMTOOLS_ARGS[@]}"} \
            --metadata '{"contextId":"${{ needs.guard.outputs.anchor }}"}' \
            --ciRunUrl "${CI_RUN_URL}" --debug 2>&1 | tee "${RUN_OUTPUT}"
          RC=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
          exit "${RC}"

      - name: Publish leg token usage (fa-tokens ledger -> factory-data)
        # Factory-board token spend (dmtools-agents#781 producer side): the
        # fa CLI prints a `fa-tokens:` ledger line per session segment into
        # the run output; sum them and append one row per leg under
        # data/fa-tokens.json on the factory-data branch — the shape the SM
        # tick's fetchTokensFromBranch consumes (card.tokens rows
        # {leg, at, prompt, completion, total}, key 'pr-N'/'issue-N').
        # Tokens are decorative: ANY miss (no ledger line, 404 first
        # publish, conflict after retries) warns and moves on — this step
        # must never redden a green leg nor gate a failed one. always():
        # the cost happened even when the agent run above failed/timed out.
        if: always()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          ANCHOR: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.anchor }}
          KIND: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.kind }}
          CONFIG: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.config }}
          RUN_OUTPUT: ${{ github.workspace }}/.dmtools/run-output.txt
          DATA_BRANCH: factory-data
          DATA_PATH: data/fa-tokens.json
        # Engine-side since dmtools-agents#940: the token-usage ledger publish
        # is SM cycle logic and ships in the factory-setup zip (pack
        # agents-rel-20261016-212752+). The awf copy is gone — this is the
        # only source now (ordered flip: pack landed first).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-setup/scripts/publish-token-usage.sh"

      - name: Mark machine job done (issue task list)
        # always(): the checkbox flips even when the agent run above timed
        # out, was cancelled, or failed — the marker can never dangle.
        # PR-anchored runs skip it (no issue task list).
        if: always() && inputs.pr == ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ inputs.issue }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          JOB_RESULT: ${{ job.status }}
        # Body: scripts/mark-job-done.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/mark-job-done.sh"

      - name: Park the lane on a provider-chain death (review runs only)
        id: provider_park
        # gh-1381 follow-up (flutter_agent_harness #2059 loop): when the review
        # agent's session died of a provider-chain exhaustion, the verdict file
        # is empty and the old flow cleared the trigger for an identical retry
        # — 14+ identical legs overnight. Instead: classify the fa trace tail,
        # PARK the lane (provider_quota label; shouldSkipForQuotaPark skips
        # every dispatch lane; the probe cadence or a human lifts), leave the
        # needs-human diagnosis to the apply step's gh-305 path on non-provider
        # misses, and fail RED so the run never reads green.
        if: ${{ always() && inputs.leg == 'review' }}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || github.token }}
          NUMBER_PR: ${{ inputs.pr }}
          NUMBER_ISSUE: ${{ inputs.issue }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          TRACE="${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/.dmtools/fa-trace.log"
          if [ -f "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-setup/outputs/pr_review.json" ] || [ -f "outputs/pr_review.json" ]; then
            echo "verdict file present — provider-park classification skipped"
            exit 0
          fi
          TAIL="$(tail -c 800 "$TRACE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
          # Classification = the gh-1087 vocabulary FAMILIES (provider-death
          # family: exhausted chain / quota & billing / 429-led outage), NOT a
          # single cause - per the loop-ideas review: one hardcoded signature
          # was rejected. Unknown tails fall through to the gh-305 path.
          if ! printf '%s' "$TAIL" | grep -qiE 'provider chain exhausted|usage[ _-]?limit|quota|billing|insufficient (credit|quota|balance)|429: rate limit|weekly .{0,12}usage limit'; then
            echo "no provider-death-family signature in the trace tail — verdict-apply path proceeds"
            exit 0
          fi
          NUM="${NUMBER_PR:-$NUMBER_ISSUE}"
          if [ -z "$NUM" ]; then
            echo "::error::provider-chain death but no ticket number — cannot park"
            exit 1
          fi
          gh issue edit "$NUM" --add-label provider_quota --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"
          gh issue comment "$NUM" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --body "🅿️ **Provider-chain exhausted — lane parked (\`provider_quota\`).** The review agent's session died of provider rate limits mid-review; re-deriving now would fail identically. The lane stays parked until the probe cadence or a human lifts the label."
          echo "::error::Provider chain exhausted — lane parked (provider_quota); verdict apply skipped (gh-1381 follow-up)"
          exit 1

      - name: Apply the review verdict (review runs only)
        # Zero-maintainer keystone: convert the review agent's verdict into
        # the label that drives the next machine step.
        #   APPROVE (+ green CI on the PR head) → pr_approved → merge
        #   CHANGES_REQUESTED / BLOCK           → agent:rework (bounded)
        # Verdict extraction walks a fallback chain (gh-305: the old silent
        # skip stranded the cycle post-review — no REQUEST_CHANGES → rework,
        # no approval → merge):
        #   pr_review.json → run output → machine-written PR comments →
        #   machine-written issue comments → LOUD failure
        # No verdict anywhere ⇒ ::error:: + needs-human + per-source
        # diagnosis comment + exit 1 (the cycle is stranded; a human must
        # label it). gh calls stay in this step; the parser stays pure —
        # pack loop/verdict.sh first (Wave 2), legacy tree
        # factory-agents/setup/review-verdict.sh fallback.
        # The CI-green gate applies to the APPROVE path only: gating rework
        # on green CI would deadlock exactly when CI is red because the code
        # needs rework. A PAT is REQUIRED for labeling (mute GITHUB_TOKEN).
        if: needs.guard.outputs.kind == 'review' && inputs.pr == ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          NUMBER: ${{ inputs.issue }}
          RUN_OUTPUT: .dmtools/run-output.txt
          MACHINE_AUTHOR: ${{ inputs.machine-author }}
          MAX_ROUNDS: ${{ env.MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS }}
        # Engine-side since dmtools-agents#935: the verdict application is SM
        # cycle logic and ships in the factory-setup zip (pack
        # agents-rel-20261016-185247+). The awf copy is gone — this is the
        # only source now (ordered flip: pack landed first).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-setup/scripts/apply-review-verdict.sh"

      - name: Close the review cycle (review runs only)
        # A review run must never re-queue itself: strip the queue label at
        # completion (removing a label fires no `labeled` event).
        if: always() && needs.guard.outputs.kind == 'review' && inputs.pr == ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

FOUND IT. The root cause:

The dmtools-agents factory pack caches per-ticket session artifacts (`copilot-session.zip`, `agent-outputs.zip`, timer snapshots) as **GitHub Release assets**, one release per ticket, tag `ai-{ticketKey}` (e.g. `ai-gh-2287`), created via `github_get_or_create_draft_release` — a **DRAFT release** keyed to the ticket. These are the "machine-account drafts" — created by ai-teammate via its token (`SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN`), outside this repo's release pipeline, no marker, no tag push.

Key observations:
1. `downloadArtefact` calls `getOrCreateRelease` EVEN ON RESTORE — i.e., the preJSAction (session restore at leg start) CREATES the draft if missing ("Find or create the shared release (if none → skip silently, first run)" — actually the comment says skip silently but the code calls getOrCreateRelease FIRST, creating the release even on restore). So every ticket leg creates a draft release `ai-gh-<issue>` (and for PR-anchored legs `ai-pr-<n>`).
2. These drafts live in the TARGET repo (resolveArtefactRepository falls back to targetRepository — IstiN/flutter_agent_harness). So the ai-gh-* drafts accumulate in THIS repo's Releases.
3. They never get published (they're draft by design — used purely as artifact storage) and never get deleted after the ticket cycle ends. They sit there, the sweper deletes them after 24h, files an issue; next day new tickets → new drafts → the sweep issue re-opens. Recurrence.

So the "bug" in THIS repo's terms (per the ticket): the sweep keeps finding stale pipeline-created drafts, filed as `[daily-publish] stale release drafts swept` — and this specific issue gh-236 will auto-close only when a sweep comes up clean. The recurrence means "a lifecycle guard is missing (issue #282)".

What's the right fix within THIS repo?

Options:
A. Teach the sweper that `ai-gh-*` / `ai-pr-*` machine-account drafts are ARTIFACT-STORAGE drafts (the factory's session/artifact cache), not failed-release drafts — and that a ticket whose cycle is CLOSED (issue closed / PR merged/closed) can never be resumed, so its draft can be swept immediately (or kept but not counted as "stale" hygiene failures?). But deleting them breaks artifact restore for closed tickets? No — if the cycle is closed, no restore will ever happen... BUT: rework legs CAN re-open? If a human re-opens the issue and reassigns, restore would find no release (the restore path handles missing release gracefully — "No existing release — skipping restore (first run)"). So sweeping them is safe-ish but loses session continuity for reopened tickets (acceptable; the sweep already deletes them after 24h anyway!).

B. The real problem the ticket highlights: RECURRENCE. The sweep deleted 6 drafts and files an issue. The next day, 5+ new drafts (fresh) will age past 24h and be swept → the issue re-opens. A lifecycle guard is missing: nothing deletes the `ai-*` artifact drafts when the ticket cycle ends.

The root-cause fix in THIS repo: add the missing lifecycle guard — when a ticket's machine cycle completes (issue closed, PR merged), the associated `ai-gh-<n>` / `ai-pr-<n>` artifact draft is no longer needed. Someone should delete it.

Where can THIS repo implement that? Ideas:
1. The daily sweep: sweep `ai-*` artifact drafts EARLY (like the gh-2318 reclaim) when the associated ticket is provably finished — issue gh-N closed, or PR #N merged/closed. That's a targeted, safe guard: fresh <24h `ai-gh-2314` whose issue #2314 is closed → delete immediately. This stops the recurrence: today's new drafts get reclaimed the same day; only drafts of tickets still in flight (<24h, open) survive, and those eventually get swept by the 24h rule anyway... but WAIT — that last part is the recurrence engine: an in-flight ticket older than 24h (e.g. a parked/blocked ticket) would get its artifact draft swept at 24h, re-creating it at the next leg... but then it's fresh again, not stale... unless the ticket stays in flight >24h with no leg — then sweep → recurrence.

Hmm. But actually, think again about what the sweper should do with `ai-*` artifact drafts: they are NOT "failed release drafts" at all. The sweep issue's prose ("a gh release create step died between asset upload and publish") is misleading for them. The 24h stale rule deleting them is fine as hygiene, but the ISSUE filing for them is noise: they recur by design as long as the machine loop runs tickets.

Wait, actually — is that true? Let me reconsider: should they be excluded from the "stale pipeline-created drafts" issue-filing logic, or should the lifecycle guard delete them at cycle end?

The ticket says: "Recurrence means a lifecycle guard is missing (issue #282)." Issue #282 is the release-draft lifecycle hygiene epic: "no pipeline step may leave a draft release behind". The missing guard here: the machine loop's artifact-cache drafts are never lifecycle-managed — created per ticket, never deleted at cycle end.

Given the constraint that the factory pack is external (dmtools-agents), the guard must live in THIS repo. The natural place: the daily sweper — it already has the reclaim machinery (gh-2318). Extend it:

**Root-cause fix:** in `sweep_stale_drafts.sh`, classify machine-account drafts carrying the artifact-cache tag shape (`ai-gh-<n>` / `ai-pr-<n>`) and reclaim (delete) them as soon as their owning ticket cycle has ENDED — issue `<n>` is closed, or PR `<n>` is merged/closed — regardless of age. This is the "lifecycle guard": a closed cycle can never restore its artifacts (no future leg will run), so the draft is provably garbage the moment the cycle ends, not 24h later.

And symmetric: the 24h stale rule stays as the backstop for cycle-still-open drafts (ticket parked forever → swept at 24h; if the ticket resumes, restore recreates the draft — self-healing).

Hmm wait, but there's a subtlety: is it correct that a CLOSED issue can never be resumed? On GitHub, issues can be REOPENED and re-assigned to ai-teammate → a new dev leg runs → restore runs → release missing → skips restore gracefully (fresh session). So deleting on close loses the old session zip — acceptable, because the sweep ALREADY deletes these after 24h today (gh-2287 made machine drafts swept). The artifact drafts are disposable caches, explicitly "best-effort" (every failure in cacheToReleases/restoreFromReleases warns and moves on). Losing one 24h→0h earlier is a minor cache-continuity change with big noise reduction.

Hmm, wait — actually let me reconsider. Is that ACTUALLY the right root-cause fix, or is the right fix to stop COUNTING ai-* drafts as "stale pipeline-created drafts" (i.e., stop filing the issue for them)?

Let me re-read the ticket once more:

"**Swept:** 6 stale pipeline-created draft(s) older than 24h — all ai-gh-*/ai-pr-* machine-account drafts. **Fresh drafts (<24h):** 5 — untouched (an in-flight run may own them). A stale draft means a `gh release create` step died between asset upload and publish — check the creating run's failed step. Recurrence means a lifecycle guard is missing (issue #282)."

The issue auto-closes when a sweep finds nothing stale. With ~5 new ticket drafts per day, this issue will NEVER auto-close — every sweep finds yesterday's ai-* drafts stale. That's the bug: a permanent, recurring red-hygiene issue generated by normal machine-loop operation, and its prose misdirects ("check the creating run's failed step" — there IS no creating run).

So the fix has two faces:
1. **Stop the misleading RCA**: the ai-* artifact-cache drafts are not failed releases. The sweep should diagnose them as artifact-cache drafts (name the owning ticket) rather than "a gh release create step died".
2. **The lifecycle guard**: reclaim the artifact draft as soon as its ticket cycle has ended (closed issue / merged-or-closed PR), instead of waiting 24h and re-filing.

With both: normal machine-loop traffic produces ZERO stale-sweep findings (drafts of in-flight tickets are fresh + alive; closed tickets get reclaimed same-day), so the sweep issue can auto-close and stay closed. Recurrence eliminated.

Now — where exactly to implement? `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh` is the sweper. Let me design:

In the bucketing jq: keep existing buckets (stale+pipeline → bot; stale+human → human; fresh → fresh). The ai-* machine drafts bucket to "bot" when stale (author == assignee). In the `bot` case branch, before deleting: check whether the tag matches the artifact-cache shape `^ai-(gh|pr)-[0-9]+$` (normalized from the ticket key — note `buildTag` lowercases and replaces non-alnum with '-', so `GH-2287` → `ai-gh-2287`, `pr-2293` → `ai-pr-2293`). If it matches:
 - Determine the owning ticket: strip `ai-` prefix, `gh-<n>` → issue #n, `pr-<n>` → PR #n.
 - If the issue/PR is CLOSED (or PR merged), delete it and report as "reclaimed (ticket cycle ended)" — count in reclaimed, with a line naming the ticket and its state.
 - If still open/merged-but-open... if PR merged, the issue will close too (Closes #N). If issue open and draft stale — keep? Hmm, if the draft is >24h stale and the ticket is still open, it means the leg has been stuck/parked for >24h — the next leg would recreate the draft on restore, so deleting is STILL safe (restore recreates). Actually for machine drafts (artifact caches), deletion at 24h is already the current behavior; keep that.

Wait, wait. Let me think about whether to keep deleting stale ai-* drafts at 24h when the ticket is still OPEN. If a ticket sits open for >24h with its session cached, the sweep deletes the draft; when the leg re-runs (retry/rework), restore recreates it (empty) — session continuity lost, but that's the CURRENT behavior too (gh-2287 made them swept at 24h). Not a regression; keep.

So the new logic: machine-account draft with tag matching `ai-(gh|pr)-<n>` →
 - If ticket closed (issue closed / PR merged or closed) → delete NOW (any age), report as reclaimed-early with the ticket state. This is the lifecycle guard — the missing piece.
 - If ticket open → behaves as today: fresh stays untouched; stale (>24h) gets swept as before.
 - Lookup failure → fail-safe keep (for the reclaim; stale ones still swept after 24h as today).

Hmm, but hold on — should the sweep STILL file the issue when it reclaims ai-* drafts? Today `reclaimed_count` counts into `stale_count`, so the issue is filed/updated with the "Reclaimed early" section. If we start reclaiming ai-* drafts of closed tickets, every daily run where a closed ticket's draft exists (i.e., any ticket closed within the last ~24h that had a machine leg) would file/comment the sweep issue → STILL recurring noise! E.g. today: 5 fresh ai-* drafts of tickets in flight; tomorrow those tickets are closed and their drafts get "reclaimed" → sweep finds "something stale" → files issue. That just replaces 24h-stale noise with same-day reclaim noise. NOT the fix.

So the lifecycle reclaim must NOT count toward the sweep issue — it's routine hygiene, not a finding. The issue should be filed only for drafts that are genuinely unexpected: failed release-train drafts (v* tags with markers, bot-author vX.Y.Z drafts) and human drafts. The ai-* artifact-cache lifecycle is normal.

Hmm, but is it? Careful: an `ai-*` draft could also be a sign of a wedged machine loop (ticket stuck open >24h). But that's what the 24h sweep is for... and if the ticket is still open, is the draft stale-garbage? The session cache of a parked ticket: if the leg gets re-armed, restore recreates. Deleting at 24h loses cache continuity for a ticket that MIGHT resume. But again: current behavior (post-gh-2287) already deletes them at 24h. Keep it — but should it file the issue?

Let me think about what makes the sweep come up clean on a normal day:
- Day N: tickets A (open, draft fresh 2h), B (open, draft fresh 10h), C closed yesterday, draft ai-gh-C 26h old... hmm wait — if we reclaim ai-* drafts of CLOSED tickets immediately at day N's sweep, ai-gh-C never lives past the first sweep after close. So at any sweep, existing ai-* drafts belong to tickets that are open (in flight or parked).
 - Parked ticket open >24h → its draft goes stale at 24h → swept → counts as stale → issue filed. Recurrence again?? Only while a ticket is genuinely parked >24h. That's a real signal (something IS stuck) but the "check the creating run's failed step" prose is still wrong for artifact drafts...

Hmm OK wait. Let me step back and reconsider the whole design. Maybe cleaner:

**Treat ai-* artifact-cache drafts as a first-class class in the sweper with their own bucket `artifacts`, and treat them as lifecycle-managed, NOT as stale-release findings:**
- Delete if: owner ticket cycle ended (closed issue / merged/closed PR) — reclaim immediately.
- Delete if: stale (>24h) — as today (backstop for parked tickets).
- Keep + count as fresh if: <24h and ticket open.
- Issue filing: hmm...

The question remains whether 24h-stale ai-* drafts of OPEN tickets should file the sweep issue. Options:
(a) They file (status quo) — parked-ticket noise recurs.
(b) They don't file — the sweep summary mentions them; the issue stays clean.

What does the ISSUE exist for? "a deduplicated self-closing issue whenever anything stale was found — a comment on the open issue instead of a duplicate, auto-closed again once a sweep comes up clean (same convention as nightly)". The issue's purpose is to surface ROT: drafts that keep roting signal a broken step. For ai-* artifact drafts, rot is BOUNDED (≤24h) and self-healing by design — the cache gets recreated per leg. The sweep deleting them at 24h is expected operation, not a defect. The only defect signal would be: ai-* drafts appearing for tickets whose legs are NOT running (open-but-idle) — a factory wedge, which OTHER issues (sm-kicker watchdogs) already surface.

Also NOTE: the ticket gh-236 itself — this auto-filed issue — says "auto-closes when a sweep finds nothing stale". If our fix makes ai-* drafts non-findings (reclaimed at cycle end + swept at 24h silently), then after this PR merges, the next sweep: ai-* drafts belong to open tickets (fresh → untouched, count only) → stale_count drops → if nothing else stale, the sweep auto-closes THIS issue. 

And for parked-ticket drafts (open ticket, stale draft): silent 24h sweep, named in the summary as artifact-cache sweeps. Hmm — but is silently deleting them RIGHT? The session cache loss for a parked ticket... The current behavior deletes them anyway. OK.

Hmm, hold on though. Let me reconsider (a) vs (b) once more by looking at what the machine loop does when a ticket is parked (provider_quota): the lane stays parked for days; the ai-gh-N draft gets swept at 24h; next leg (human lifts) → restore recreates → fresh again. Under (a), every parked ticket generates recurring sweep issues — that's the exact noise class we're killing. Under (b), no issue. I'm fairly confident (b) is right for ai-* drafts: they are caches, not releases; their lifecycle is managed; deleting an old cache is maintenance, not an incident.

BUT — I must be careful not to swallow REAL signal: what if the machine loop starts creating ai-* drafts with BROKEN assets (upload failures leave empty drafts)? Those still get deleted silently. Meh — cache loss is harmless (the pack handles missing caches gracefully; restore "first run" path is a no-op). Fine.

Also, hmm, one more angle: is deleting ai-* drafts of closed tickets even MY business vs. adding a guard to the machine loop? The pack (`cacheToReleases.js`/`restoreFromReleases.js`) is in dmtools-agents (external). The ticket in THIS repo expects a fix in THIS repo. The sweper is this repo's hygiene leg and the established home for draft lifecycle rules (gh-2287, gh-2318 both landed there). So yes: fix the sweper.

Now let me nail the exact classification. Tag shapes produced by buildTag: lowercase, [^a-z0-9._/-]→'-'. For GitHub tracker ticket keys: gh-2287 → `ai-gh-2287`; pr-2293 → `ai-pr-2293`. Note the dot/slash are allowed chars in buildTag but GitHub issue keys here are gh-N/pr-N so shape is `ai-(gh|pr)-[0-9]+`. 

BUT WAIT — careful: the gh-2287 fix bucketed drafts by AUTHOR == assignee, which also matches OTHER machine drafts (e.g. any draft the ai-teammate account ever creates — including potential future vX.Y.Z drafts if the machine ever pushes tags). The artifact-cache classification should key on the TAG SHAPE (ai-gh-<digits>/ai-pr-<digits>), not just author. A machine draft named v1.0.750 would stay in the old "bot" bucket. Good separation:

- bucket `artifacts`: author == assignee AND tag matches `^ai-(gh|pr)-[0-9]+$` → lifecycle-managed artifact-cache draft.
 - If ticket closed → delete now (reclaimed; NOT counted in stale_count).
 - If stale (>24h) → delete (backstop, named in summary; NOT counted in stale_count... hmm — decide: not counted).
 - Else fresh+open → untouched, counted in fresh_count (or its own counter).
- bucket `bot` (existing): pipeline drafts NOT matching the artifact shape (marker'd vX.Y.Z, bot-author vX.Y.Z, machine-account vX.Y.Z) → delete + issue as today.

Hmm, hmm. Wait — but do I really want artifact sweeps to be silent? Let me look at the gh-2318 precedent again: reclaimed_count DOES count toward stale_count and files the issue — because those were REAL v*-tag staging drafts whose publish point died. Different class. For artifact caches, silent is right...

Hmm, actually, let me reconsider once more. Is it possible the RIGHT fix is different: maybe the artifact drafts should just NOT BE DELETED AT ALL by this repo's sweper, because they're the machine loop's live cache (a ticket in review/rework may be days old and need its session zip!). Deleting at 24h already loses that today — but nobody complained? Hmm, wait — actually, IS session continuity actually used? The fa session rides the fa-sess/gh-<n> GIT BRANCH ("fa sessions ride the fa-sess/gh-<n> branch"), NOT the release cache! The factory comment says: "actions/cache saves are denied on issues-event runs; fa sessions ride the fa-sess/gh-<n> branch". So what's in the ai-* release cache then? `copilot-session.zip, agent-outputs.zip, ...` — copilot artifacts (Copilot agent sessions), agent outputs. For fa runner legs, maybe NOTHING gets cached (no copilot) — yet drafts are CREATED (empty!) because BOTH cacheToReleases AND restoreFromReleases call getOrCreateRelease unconditionally!! That's exactly why these drafts are EMPTY (no assets) — swept drafts show no assets mentioned.

Let me verify: does cacheToReleases.js only create the release when there are assets to upload? Let me fetch it and restoreFromReleases.js.

I now understand the test conventions fully. Important detail in the gh-2287 test: `'ai-pr-210'` — the existing test uses `ai-pr-210` (issue 210? no — pr 210). And the gh-2287 test asserts stale machine drafts ARE deleted AND the issue IS filed (that's current behavior: machine drafts are bot-bucketed and issue-filing counts them).

My change alters that behavior for machine drafts with ai-(gh|pr)-N tags: they move to the new artifacts bucket. The EXISTING gh-2287 test will need updating — wait, no: my fix must be careful here. The gh-2287 test has:
- `ai-gh-2208` stale → currently swept + issue filed naming it.
- `ai-pr-210` stale → swept + named.
- `ai-gh-219` fresh → untouched.

With my fix, if the ticket state is unknown (no issue fixtures), what happens? My design:
- stale artifact draft with ticket CLOSED → early reclaim (silent).
- stale artifact draft with ticket OPEN or lookup-failed → backstop sweep — SILENT (no issue count)?? 

Hmm — wait. This CHANGES the existing gh-2287 behavior: today a stale machine draft files the issue. If I make artifact sweeps silent, then a stale ai-gh-2208 (ticket state unknown in the test) would be deleted but the issue NOT filed → the existing gh-2287 test FAILS (it expects `issue create` and body naming ai-gh-2208).

Hmm. So I need to decide: is silently deleting stale artifact drafts correct? Let me reconsider...

Actually — wait. Let me reconsider the design. What does "correct" mean for this ticket? The ticket says recurrence of stale ai-* drafts = missing lifecycle guard. The proper lifecycle: the artifact draft should die when the ticket cycle ends. After my fix, in steady state (every machine ticket's issue closes when its PR merges), drafts get reclaimed promptly at the next daily sweep and — importantly — they're no longer FINDINGS. The sweep issue auto-closes when only artifact drafts flow through.

But hold on — should a stale artifact draft with ticket still OPEN count as a finding? Consider the actual failure mode it represents: the machine loop created a draft and the ticket is still open >24h. The draft is NOT stale garbage per se... the leg may resume. The 24h backstop delete loses session cache for a resumable ticket. Hmm, is deleting it at 24h even right? It's today's behavior (bot bucket). Keep it as-is but silent.

So the existing gh-2287 test expectations change for ai-* drafts: deleted (backstop) but NOT issue-filing. The test asserts issue IS filed naming ai-gh-2208... I'd need to UPDATE that test to the new contract (the ai-* rows move out of the issue-finding class). That's expected — the behavior contract changes. The test's human rows (v0.2.0, v0.3.0) still file the issue via the human bucket — actually yes! The gh-2287 test has a stale human draft `v0.2.0` (kept) and look-alike `v0.3.0` (kept) — those still count → issue still filed. So the issue body would list v0.2.0/v0.3.0 but NOT ai-gh-2208/ai-pr-210. The test needs rework: delete assertions stay (backstop still deletes stale ai-* drafts), body assertions change (ai-* no longer named in the issue), fresh stays untouched.

Hmm wait — but actually, hold on. Should the STALE ai-* (ticket open) still be deleted silently? What if the ticket is open because the machine loop is WORKING on it right now (leg in flight for >24h — the 260min cap says no; legs cap at ~4.3h)? >24h open with no leg = parked/blocked. Deleting the cache is fine (restore recreates). But SILENTLY? The parked ticket itself is tracked by its own issue + labels (needs-human etc.). I'm OK with silent.

Hmm, but hmm, wait. Now I realize there may be an even better approach for the "stale + open" case: leave it ALONE (don't delete!). Think: today's bot-bucket deletes machine drafts >24h. Why? Because a >24h-old machine draft is presumed abandoned pipeline garbage. For artifact caches that presumption is WRONG — an open ticket's cache is still potentially resumable! The truly-garbage artifact drafts are those whose cycle ENDED (closed) — and those get reclaimed by the guard immediately. So for artifacts I could:
- closed ticket → reclaim NOW (the guard).
- open ticket, any age → KEEP (cache may be needed; it's lifecycle-managed, not rot).
- unknown (lookup failed) → KEEP (fail-safe; retried next sweep).

That would ALSO stop the daily re-file: today the loop's parked tickets keep generating new drafts... wait no — with "open → keep", a parked ticket's draft sits forever?? No — when the ticket eventually closes (human triage), the guard reclaims it next sweep. And if a ticket stays open forever, one draft sits forever — but it's not a FINDING either (silent summary mention). Hmm, but then "Fresh drafts (<24h): 5" would become a growing pile of ai-* drafts of open tickets... which is FINE — they're the machine loop's live caches, exactly like the fa-sess/* git branches (which also accumulate one branch per ticket forever!).

Hmm, hmm. Decision between:
(A) open+stale → delete (today's behavior, silent): parked ticket loses cache (recoverable — restore recreates), no unbounded growth. 
(B) open+any-age → keep: cache preserved for parked tickets (matches the fa-sess branch pattern), no growth of FINDINGS; growth of quiet artifact drafts bounded by open tickets.

Which is more true to the ticket? The ticket's complaint: stale ai-* swept + recurring issue. Under (A), parked-ticket drafts still get swept daily (recurring sweep activity but SILENT — no issue). Under (B), they're kept — the sweep only ever reclaims closed-cycle drafts.

Hmm, wait — actually there's a subtle danger in (B): the ai-* drafts would then NEVER be swept for stuck-open tickets (zombie tickets nobody closes) — unbounded accumulation of draft releases. Drafts are invisible in the releases UI until... actually drafts are visible to maintainers in the Releases page. A zombie leak. Under (A), the 24h backstop bounds every artifact draft's life to max(ticket-open time, 24h-after-close... no— reclaim-at-close). Hmm, under (A) + guard: every artifact draft dies at close; open tickets' drafts die at 24h. Total bounded: ≤ #open tickets + ~1 day of closed tickets. Nice hygiene.

Under (A), the cache-loss risk: a ticket parked 3 days, then human lifts provider_quota → leg resumes → restore finds nothing → fresh session (the pack's contract handles it: "first run"). What does session loss cost? The fa session ALSO rides fa-sess/gh-<n> git branch (the factory comment: sessions ride the branch — the release cache is for COPILOT artifacts and timer snapshots of CLI OUTPUT, not the fa session tree). So the release cache is auxiliary (output snapshots, agent outputs). Losing it is cheap. Under (B) the cost of keeping: zombie drafts accumulate.

Given the repo's hygiene philosophy (#282: "no pipeline step may leave a draft release behind"; the sweep deletes stale drafts as BACKSTOP), (A) is more consistent: keep the 24h backstop for open tickets, add the close-guard. And (A) preserves today's deletion semantics — minimal behavioral change: machine ai-* drafts still get deleted (>24h or closed), just correctly classified + no longer issue-findings + reclaimed EARLY at cycle end.

Now — what about a machine ai-* draft for a ticket that's closed but <24h old? (A) reclaims immediately. That's the guard: cycle ended → no leg will ever restore it... wait, can a leg restore after close? A rework leg could be dispatched after the issue closes? The rework cycle closes the label at leg end; rework legs run while the PR/issue is open. After close, could a human re-open + reassign → NEW dev leg → restore → cache gone → fresh session. Acceptable (documented in the comment).

OK — design settled (option A + close-guard). Now the summary/issue-body treatment:

New accumulators:
- `art_reclaimed` / `art_reclaimed_tags` — closed-cycle reclaims (silent, but named in summary AND in the issue body IF an issue is filed for other findings — hmm, or also comment? Keep: only in body when filing happens anyway; always in summary).
- `art_swept` / `art_swept_tags` — stale open-ticket backstop sweeps (silent).
- `art_kept` / `art_kept_tags` — fresh/open artifact drafts (kept) — summary only. Hmm — name them clearly: "artifact-cache drafts kept (ticket in flight)".

Counting for `stale_count` (issue filing): unchanged components (deleted bot/human/marker + gh-2318 reclaimed + humans). Artifacts excluded.

Wait — hmm, one more scenario: TODAY's gh-2287 test asserts `run.body` contains `ai-gh-2208` etc. — with my change the issue body no longer names artifact drafts... unless the issue is filed for other reasons and I include the artifact section there. I planned to include artifact lines in the body when filed anyway. In the gh-2287 test, the human drafts (v0.2.0, v0.3.0 kept) file the issue → body contains artifact section with ai-gh-2208/ai-pr-210 lines (swept backstop) — hmm, then `contains('ai-gh-2208')` still passes!
