# Root Cause Analysis — gh-236 `[daily-publish] stale release drafts swept`

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The daily draft-sweep issue keeps recurring (gh-2287 → gh-2318 → gh-236): every machine-loop ticket leg leaves a stale `ai-gh-<n>` / `ai-pr-<n>` draft release behind, the sweep deletes it only after 24h and files/updates the recurring sweep issue, so the issue can never auto-close and the next day's tickets re-open it.

**Root cause**: `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh` has no lifecycle for the machine loop's **artefact-cache draft class**. The dmtools-agents factory (`js/timerAutoCommitAndSave.js` → `js/common/releaseArtefacts.js` → `github_get_or_create_draft_release`, tag template `ai-{ticketKey}`) writes every fa leg's session/output snapshots as assets of a per-ticket **draft** release `ai-gh-<n>` / `ai-pr-<n>` in this repo, created with the ai-teammate token (User-typed, marker-less — no `release-draft-owner` marker, no Actions run owns it). These drafts are caches by design (never published, safe to delete), but the sweeper's only bucket for them is the generic post-gh-2287 `bot` bucket: swept after 24h AND counted as sweep findings (`stale_count`), so normal machine-loop traffic perpetually files the issue. The missing lifecycle guard (issue #282): **an artefact draft is garbage the moment its ticket cycle ends** (issue closed / PR merged-or-closed — a closed cycle never resumes; the pack's restore path is non-fatal and recreates on "first run"), and nothing reclaims it then — it rots 24h and re-files the issue. The issue prose also misdirects RCA for this class ("a `gh release create` step died between asset upload and publish — check the creating run's failed step") — there is no creating run and nothing died.

**Impact**: Recurring release-hygiene noise (6 drafts swept in gh-236, ~5 fresh behind them), a permanently re-filed sweep issue that auto-close can never clear, a wrong diagnosis in the issue for every machine draft, and 24h+ of rotted cache drafts that a cycle-end guard would have reclaimed the same day.

**Fix approach**: In `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh`, classify machine-account (`$DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE`) drafts whose tag matches `ai-(gh|pr)-<digits>` into a dedicated `artifacts` bucket with its own lifecycle: (1) reclaim immediately — any age — when the ticket entity (`gh api repos/$repo/issues/<n>`) is `closed`; (2) keep the existing 24h backstop sweep when the ticket is still open (parked leg; the cache is recreated if the leg resumes); (3) keep fresh+open drafts untouched (in-flight leg may own them); (4) exclude the class from `stale_count` so the sweep issue auto-closes when only cache traffic remains; (5) fail-safe: any ticket-state lookup failure keeps the draft (no blind deletes) and only the 24h backstop applies. Non-matching machine drafts (e.g. a machine-authored `vX.Y.Z` train draft) stay in the `bot` bucket and remain findings; human-authored `ai-*` drafts stay protected by E1.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — first fix for this ticket. Related prior fixes: gh-2287 (PR #2289) made machine-account drafts sweepable at all (they previously rotted forever as "human"); gh-2318 (PR #2319) added early reclaim for fresh *release-train* drafts with a dead tag train — neither gives the machine-loop cache class a lifecycle, so the sweep issue keeps recurring (this ticket).

# The machine loop (dmtools-agents factory: timerAutoCommitAndSave.js →
# releaseArtefacts.uploadRawFile → github_get_or_create_draft_release, tag
# template `ai-{ticketKey}`) writes every fa leg's session/output snapshots

# with the ai-teammate token — User-typed, marker-less, no Actions run owns
# it. Those drafts are caches by design (never published, assets
# best-effort), NOT failed release-train drafts — but without a lifecycle
# they rotted 24h, were swept as generic bot-bucket findings, and re-filed
# the recurring sweep issue every day (gh-2287 → gh-2318 → gh-236). The
# guard: a machine-account draft whose tag matches `ai-(gh|pr)-<digits>` is
#   - RECLAIMED NOW, any age, when the ticket entity is `closed` — a closed
#     cycle never resumes (a reopened ticket starts a fresh session; the
#     pack's restore path is non-fatal and recreates the cache on "first
#     run"), so the draft is provably garbage the moment the cycle ends;
#   - swept by the existing 24h backstop when the ticket is still open (a
#     parked leg — the cache is recreated if the leg resumes);
#   - kept untouched while the ticket is open and the draft is fresh (an
#     in-flight leg may be writing snapshots into it);
#   - KEPT on any ticket-state lookup failure (never delete blind) — only
#     the 24h backstop then applies.
# The class is EXCLUDED from the sweep-issue finding counters: reclaiming a
# lifecycle-managed cache is routine hygiene, not a stale-draft finding, so
# the issue auto-closes when only cache traffic remains. Human-authored
# `ai-*` drafts are NOT lifecycle-managed (E1 holds — they stay listed,
# kept), and machine-authored non-matching drafts (e.g. a machine-authored
# `vX.Y.Z` train draft) stay in the bot bucket and remain findings.

# never-publishable: the v1.0.739 shape — a daily-child staging leg
      # minted the tag (release_tag_mint.sh) and staged the draft, the
      # freshly fired train failed upstream of release-provenance, and the
      # gh-2230 train-draft-guard either ran before the draft existed (a
      # long attach leg created it later) or kept it while its owner was
      # still in-flight. Nothing re-examined such a draft with train
      # knowledge, so it rotted the full 24h and re-filed the recurring
      # sweep issue. Apply the train guard's EXACT criterion here —
      # reclaim only a well-formed-marker draft whose owner run COMPLETED,
      # whose tag has NO queued/in-flight ci.yml push train, and whose
      # newest concluded ci.yml push train failed with release-provenance
      # SKIPPED (rerun --failed cannot resurrect skipped jobs — nobody
      # will ever publish it). Fail-safe keeps mirror the train guard:
      # unmarked/human drafts (E1), an in-flight owner run (possibly
      # mid-upload), ANY queued/in-flight tag train (it may still publish
      # even when an older train failed), a rerunnable FAILED provenance
      # (that draft stays the `rerun --failed` recovery vessel, gh-1899,
      # until the stale sweep), any lookup failure (never delete blind),
      # and untagged drafts (no train to diagnose).
      if [ -n "$marker_run" ] && [ "$tag" != "(untagged)" ]; then
        owner_status=$(gh run view "$marker_run" --repo "$repo" --json status 2>/dev/null \
          | jq -r '.status // empty' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
        if [ "$owner_status" = "completed" ]; then
          diag=$(train_diagnosis "$tag")
          train_url_found=$(printf '%s' "$diag" | cut -f3)
          failed_jobs=$(printf '%s' "$diag" | cut -f4)
          prov_conclusion=$(printf '%s' "$diag" | cut -f5)
          train_conclusion=$(printf '%s' "$diag" | cut -f2)
          train_in_flight=$(printf '%s' "$diag" | cut -f6)
          if [ -n "$diag" ] && [ "$prov_conclusion" = "skipped" ] \
            && [ "$train_in_flight" = "none" ]; then
            gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id" >/dev/null
            reclaimed_count=$((reclaimed_count + 1))
            failed_trains=$((failed_trains + 1))
            run_url="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL:-https://github.com}/$repo/actions/runs/$marker_run"
            train_line="  - tag train: ${train_url_found:-<url unavailable>} concluded ${train_conclusion:-unknown} — the staged draft was never published (release-provenance, the sole publish point, is gated behind the tag train; a superseded failed train is never rerun — verify_pubdev_release.sh heals the LATEST tag only)"
            [ -n "$failed_jobs" ] && train_line="$train_line; failed jobs: $failed_jobs"
            reclaimed="$reclaimed- \`$tag\` — created $created by @$author; creating run: $run_url\n  - reclaimed early: the draft is younger than $((max_age / 3600))h but its publish point is unreachable (failed train, skipped release-provenance — rerun --failed cannot resurrect skipped jobs), so no in-flight run can own it and nobody will ever publish it (gh-2318)\n$train_line\n"
            reclaimed_tags="$reclaimed_tags $tag"
            continue
          fi
        fi
      fi

      ;;

      humans="$humans- \`$tag\` — created $created by @$author (human draft: listed, kept)\n"
      human_tags="$human_tags $tag"
      ;;
    bot)
      gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id" >/dev/null
      deleted_count=$((deleted_count + 1))

      # broken step instead of rotting silently (AC2). Marker drafts name

      # author-bot drafts fall back to the newest run on the tag ref;
      # dispatch-time drafts have no run on their ref — then say so.

          --json url --jq '.[0].url // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)

          # "creating step died mid-run" prose below would misdirect the
          # RCA (gh-2105 class) — nothing died.

  --description "Auto-filed by the release-draft sweeper" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# ── inventory ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gh api --paginate emits one JSON array per page; the jq stream filter
# flattens them all. Bucketing happens in jq so the whole rule is
# reviewable in one place:
#   artifacts (machine account + ai-(gh|pr)-<n> tag — gh-236)
#                    -> lifecycle-managed: reclaim at cycle end / 24h
#                    backstop / keep in flight; NEVER a sweep finding
#   stale + pipeline (bot author, the machine account, or well-formed
#                    release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<job>
#                    marker in the body) -> delete, name the marker run
#   stale + human (no marker)          -> keep, list
#   fresh                              -> untouched, EXCEPT the gh-2318
#                    reclaim: a marked draft whose owner run completed and
#                    whose tag's train failed with release-provenance
#                    SKIPPED (publish point unreachable) is deleted NOW
drafts=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$repo/releases" | jq -r --argjson maxage "$max_age" --arg assignee "$assignee" '
  [ .[] | select(.draft == true)
    | { stale: ((now - (.created_at | fromdateiso8601)) > $maxage),
        bucket: (
          # gh-236 first: the machine loop's artefact-cache class, keyed on
          # the machine account AND the `ai-{ticketKey}` tag shape the
          # factory's releaseArtefacts.buildTag() produces (lowercased,
          # non-alnum → '-', so `GH-2288` → `ai-gh-2288`, `pr-2293` →
          # `ai-pr-2293`). Human-authored ai-* drafts and machine-authored
          # vX.Y.Z drafts never match and fall through to the buckets below.
          if (((.author.login // "") == $assignee)
              and ((.tag_name // "") | test("^ai-(gh|pr)-[0-9]+$")))
          then "artifacts"
          elif ((now - (.created_at | fromdateiso8601)) > $maxage)
          then (if ((.author.type // "User") == "Bot"
                    or ((.author.login // "") | test("\\[bot\\]$"))
                    or ((.author.login // "") == $assignee)
                    or ((.body // "") | test("release-draft-owner: run/[0-9]+/job/")))
               then "bot" else "human" end)
          else "fresh" end),
        tag: (.tag_name // "(untagged)"),
        id: (.id | tostring),
        created: (.created_at // "?"),
        author: (.author.login // "unknown"),

— a failed **or cancelled** run deletes its orphaned draft instead of
  leaving it to rot. The delete is **ownership-scoped** (review of #294):
  the guard only deletes a draft whose body carries this very run+job's
  `<!-- release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<job> -->` marker — daily-publish
  runs the mobile and macOS legs concurrently on the same derived tag, and
  a failed leg's guard must never destroy the sibling leg's mid-upload
  draft (foreign or unmarked drafts are left to the sweeper). Pinned by
  `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` (a job with an asset-carrying create
  and no guard fails CI).
- **Train-level draft lifecycle guard** (gh-2230) — the per-job guards
  above fire only on their own job's failure, but since the gh-1801
  rework the staged draft's publish owner is the TAG TRAIN (ci.yml's
  `release-provenance`, the sole publish point). A train that dies
  upstream of the publish point (core tests → quality-gate red → binaries
  skipped → provenance skipped) used to orphan the staged draft until the
  24h sweeper reclaimed it and filed the recurring sweep issue. ci.yml now
  carries a `train-draft-guard` job (`needs: release-provenance`,
  `if: always()` on tag-push/release events) running
  `scripts/release_train_draft_guard.sh` with the publish point's settled
  result exported. It deletes ONLY when that result is `skipped` (the
  publish point is unreachable — `rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped
  jobs): drafts for the trained tag whose well-formed ownership marker
  names a COMPLETED run go away (a superseded failed train is never rerun,
  so nobody else would ever publish them; the git tag is untouched). A
  FAILED or CANCELLED provenance is rerunnable, so the staged draft stays
  as the `rerun --failed` recovery vessel (gh-1899 convention). Fail-safe
  keeps — in-flight owner runs (a concurrent creator leg may be
  mid-upload), unmarked/human drafts (E1), any owner-status lookup failure
  (never delete blind), and an unexported result; the sweeper remains the
  backstop. Grants `contents: write` + `actions: read`, same
  stub-enforced model as the sweep-drafts job.
- **Attach-or-create** — the draft-capable creates of build-macos.yml /
  build-mobile.yml live in `scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh`, which is
  idempotent under the view→create race (#282 E3): a create that loses to
  a concurrent winner uploads into the winner's release instead of
  failing (a failing create would fire the guard against the winner's
  in-flight draft), and the create stamps the ownership marker the guard
  verifies.
- **Daily sweeper** — the `sweep-drafts` job in `daily-publish.yml` runs
  `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh` on **every** daily invocation (leg
  results and change-gating never gate hygiene): drafts older than 24h
  are deleted when the PIPELINE created them — a Bot author / `*[bot]`
  login, or the body carries a well-formed
  `release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<job>` marker (the drafts
  are created with the owner's RELEASE_PAT, so the API author is a human
  and the marker is the only ownership proof — gh-2008; the bucket rule
  keys on the exact stamped shape, so prose merely mentioning the
  substring or a malformed marker stays human — review thread
  PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6yOzIh; id-based API
  delete, tag and git history untouched — draft assets are unpublished by
  definition, E2), human drafts (no marker) are listed but kept (E1),
  fresh (<24h) drafts are left for their in-flight run — EXCEPT the
  gh-2318 early reclaim: a fresh draft whose well-formed marker names a
  COMPLETED run is deleted immediately when no ci.yml push train on the
  tag is queued/in-flight and the tag's newest concluded ci.yml push train

  (never delete blind). The job grants
  `actions: read` — unmarked swept drafts name their creating run via

- **Naming** — titles are the bare `vX.Y.Z` tag everywhere (matches the
  tag, matches pub.dev). No `Fa ` prefixes, no untitled creates; both are
  lint-failed by `test/release_hygiene_test.dart`. Pre-existing published
  titles (e.g. `Fa v0.1.362`) are deliberately not rewritten — backfill
  is opt-in per release.
- **Latest** — every publish path passes `--latest` explicitly (and
  re-asserts it via `gh release edit --latest` when attaching to a
  release another path created first). Guards and the sweeper only ever
  delete — a failed run can never capture the badge.
- **Notes** — `scripts/release_notes.sh` renders the curated CHANGELOG.md
  `## <version>` section when one exists, else the curated `## Unreleased`
  body (gh-1522: the release folds Unreleased into the tag's section at
  stage time, never in-repo), else conventional commits since the
  previous tag grouped Features/Fixes/Maintenance (capped at 50 +
  "…and N more"), with a clean "No changes" body for re-tags. The literal
  `Release vX.Y.Z` filler bodies are gone.

--- a/scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh
+++ b/scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh
@@ -33,6 +33,34 @@
 #     instead of a duplicate, auto-closed again once a sweep comes up
 #     clean (same convention as nightly.yml / daily_publish_report.sh).
 #
+# ── artefact-cache drafts have their own lifecycle (gh-236) ────────────────
+# The machine loop (dmtools-agents factory: timerAutoCommitAndSave.js →
+# releaseArtefacts.uploadRawFile → github_get_or_create_draft_release, tag
+# template `ai-{ticketKey}`) writes every fa leg's session/output snapshots
+# as assets of a per-ticket DRAFT release `ai-gh-<n>` / `ai-pr-<n>`, created
+# with the ai-teammate token — User-typed, marker-less, no Actions run owns
+# it. Those drafts are caches by design (never published, assets
+# best-effort), NOT failed release-train drafts — but without a lifecycle
+# they rotted 24h, were swept as generic bot-bucket findings, and re-filed
+# the recurring sweep issue every day (gh-2287 → gh-2318 → gh-236). The
+# guard: a machine-account draft whose tag matches `ai-(gh|pr)-<digits>` is
+#   - RECLAIMED NOW, any age, when the ticket entity is `closed` — a closed
+#     cycle never resumes (a reopened ticket starts a fresh session; the
+#     pack's restore path is non-fatal and recreates the cache on "first
+#     run"), so the draft is provably garbage the moment the cycle ends;
+#   - swept by the existing 24h backstop when the ticket is still open (a
+#     parked leg — the cache is recreated if the leg resumes);
+#   - kept untouched while the ticket is open and the draft is fresh (an
+#     in-flight leg may be writing snapshots into it);
+#   - KEPT on any ticket-state lookup failure (never delete blind) — only
+#     the 24h backstop then applies.
+# The class is EXCLUDED from the sweep-issue finding counters: reclaiming a
+# lifecycle-managed cache is routine hygiene, not a stale-draft finding, so
+# the issue auto-closes when only cache traffic remains. Human-authored
+# `ai-*` drafts are NOT lifecycle-managed (E1 holds — they stay listed,
+# kept), and machine-authored non-matching drafts (e.g. a machine-authored
+# `vX.Y.Z` train draft) stay in the bot bucket and remain findings.
+#
 # Drafts are deleted by release id via the API: a draft may carry an empty
 # tag_name, which makes every tag-based `gh release delete` ambiguous.
 #
@@ -110,6 +138,9 @@ gh label create "$label" --repo "$repo" --color B60205 \
 # gh api --paginate emits one JSON array per page; the jq stream filter
 # flattens them all. Bucketing happens in jq so the whole rule is
 # reviewable in one place:
+#   artifacts (machine account + ai-(gh|pr)-<n> tag — gh-236)
+#                    -> lifecycle-managed: reclaim at cycle end / 24h
+#                    backstop / keep in flight; NEVER a sweep finding
 #   stale + pipeline (bot author, the machine account, or well-formed
 #                    release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<job>
 #                    marker in the body) -> delete, name the marker run
@@ -120,8 +151,19 @@ gh label create "$label" --repo "$repo" --color B60205 \
 #                    SKIPPED (publish point unreachable) is deleted NOW
 drafts=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$repo/releases" | jq -r --argjson maxage "$max_age" --arg assignee "$assignee" '
   [ .[] | select(.draft == true)
-    | { bucket: (
-          if ((now - (.created_at | fromdateiso8601)) > $maxage)
+    | { stale: ((now - (.created_at | fromdateiso8601)) > $maxage),
+        bucket: (
+          # gh-236 first: the machine loop artefact-cache class, keyed on
+          # the machine account AND the `ai-{ticketKey}` tag shape the
+          # factory releaseArtefacts.buildTag() produces (lowercased,
+          # non-alnum to '-', so `GH-2288` becomes `ai-gh-2288`,
+          # `pr-2293` becomes `ai-pr-2293`). Human-authored ai-* drafts and
+          # machine-authored vX.Y.Z drafts never match and fall through to
+          # the buckets below.
+          if (((.author.login // "") == $assignee)
+              and ((.tag_name // "") | test("^ai-(gh|pr)-[0-9]+$")))
+          then "artifacts"
+          elif ((now - (.created_at | fromdateiso8601)) > $maxage)
           then (if ((.author.type // "User") == "Bot"
                     or ((.author.login // "") | test("\\[bot\\]$"))
                     or ((.author.login // "") == $assignee)
@@ -143,7 +185,10 @@ drafts=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$repo/releases" | jq -r --argjson maxage "$max
                 | .run ]
               | .[0] // "") } ]
   | sort_by(.created)[]
-  | [ .bucket, .tag, .id, .created, .author, .run ] | @tsv')
+  # Column order matters: `read` collapses runs of whitespace IFS chars, so
+  # the only possibly-EMPTY field (.run — marker-less drafts) must stay
+  # LAST; .stale sits before it (gh-236: the artifacts branch branches on it).
+  | [ .bucket, .tag, .id, .created, .author, .stale, .run ] | @tsv')
 
 deleted=""
 deleted_tags=""
@@ -158,10 +203,51 @@ reclaimed_count=0
 humans=""
 human_tags=""
 fresh_count=0
+# gh-236: machine-loop artefact-cache drafts — lifecycle-managed, NOT
+# sweep findings (reclaiming a cache whose ticket cycle ended is routine
+# hygiene; the issue must auto-close when only cache traffic remains).
+#   reclaimed at cycle end (ticket closed, any age) / swept by the 24h
+#   backstop (ticket still open / state unknown) / kept (fresh + open).
+art_reclaimed=""
+art_reclaimed_tags=""
+art_reclaimed_count=0
+art_swept=""
+art_swept_tags=""
+art_swept_count=0
+art_kept_tags=""
+art_kept_count=0
 
-while IFS=$'\t' read -r bucket tag id created author marker_run; do
+while IFS=$'\t' read -r bucket tag id created author stale marker_run; do
   [ -n "$bucket" ] || continue
   case "$bucket" in
+    artifacts)
+      # gh-236: the machine loop's per-ticket artefact-cache draft
+      # (`ai-gh-<n>` / `ai-pr-<n>` — timerAutoCommitAndSave.js snapshot
+      # storage). The tag shape was validated by the jq bucket rule, so
+      # `gh #<num>` / `pr #<num>` parsing below is total. State lookup:
+      # the issues REST API serves PRs too (state=closed covers merged).
+      # Any lookup failure yields an empty state — fail-safe: no early
+      # reclaim, only the 24h backstop below may delete.

+      kind="${rest%%-*}"
+      num="${rest##*-}"

+        | jq -r '.state // ""' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
+      if [ "$state" = "closed" ]; then
+        gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id" >/dev/null
+        art_reclaimed_count=$((art_reclaimed_count + 1))
+        art_reclaimed="$art_reclaimed- \`$tag\` — created $created by @$author; ticket cycle ended (\`$kind #$num\` closed) — reclaimed at cycle end, no 24h wait: a closed cycle never resumes and the cache is recreated on any future first run (gh-236)\n"
+        art_reclaimed_tags="$art_reclaimed_tags $tag"
+      elif [ "$stale" = "true" ]; then
+        gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id" >/dev/null
+        art_swept_count=$((art_swept_count + 1))
+        art_swept="$art_swept- \`$tag\` — created $created by @$author; swept after 24h with the ticket still open (parked leg — the cache is recreated if the leg resumes; gh-236)\n"
+        art_swept_tags="$art_swept_tags $tag"
+      else
+        art_kept_count=$((art_kept_count + 1))
+        art_kept_tags="$art_kept_tags $tag"
+      fi
+      ;;
     fresh)
       # gh-2318: "fresh — untouched" is right while an in-flight run may
       # own the draft, but a fresh draft can already be PROVABLY
@@ -297,15 +383,33 @@ if [ "$stale_count" -gt 0 ]; then
       printf '%b' "$reclaimed"
     fi
     [ -n "$humans" ] && { echo; echo "**Kept (human drafts, listed not deleted — E1):**"; printf '%b' "$humans"; }
+    # gh-236: cache lifecycle activity rides the filed issue for
+    # visibility — in its own section, with the release-failure prose
+    # never attached (nothing died, nothing failed to publish). It does
+    # NOT contribute to the finding count above.
+    if [ "$((art_reclaimed_count + art_swept_count))" -gt 0 ]; then
+      echo
+      echo "**Artefact-cache drafts (machine-loop \`ai-gh-*\`/\`ai-pr-*\` caches — lifecycle-managed, not release failures):** $art_reclaimed_count reclaimed at cycle end, $art_swept_count swept after 24h"
+      printf '%b' "$art_reclaimed"
+      printf '%b' "$art_swept"

+    elif [ "$deleted_count" -gt 0 ]; then

arguments.content:
### Root Cause
The daily draft sweeper kept re-filing "stale release drafts swept" (gh-2287 → gh-2318 → gh-236) because every machine-loop leg leaves a per-ticket **artefact-cache draft release** `ai-gh-<n>` / `ai-pr-<n>` in the repo — the dmtools-agents factory writes each fa leg's session/output snapshots into it (`github_get_or_create_draft_release`, tag template `ai-{ticketKey}`, authored by ai-teammate, marker-less, no owning run). The sweeper had no lifecycle for that class: it swept the drafts only after 24h **and counted them as sweep findings**, so normal machine-loop traffic perpetually re-opened the issue with a wrong diagnosis ("a `gh release create` step died…" — nothing died; these caches are never meant to publish).

### Fix
- `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh`: new `artifacts` bucket for machine-account drafts whose tag matches `ai-(gh|pr)-<digits>` with a real lifecycle —
  - ticket entity `closed` (issues REST API; covers merged PRs) → **reclaimed immediately, any age** (a closed cycle never resumes; the pack's restore is non-fatal and recreates the cache on first run);
  - ticket still open, draft >24h → existing 24h backstop sweep (parked leg);
  - fresh + open → kept (an in-flight leg may be writing snapshots);
  - ticket-state lookup failure → fail-safe keep (never delete blind);
  - the class is excluded from the issue-filing counters, so the recurring sweep issue finally auto-closes when only cache traffic remains; E1 holds for human-authored `ai-*` drafts, and machine-authored `vX.Y.Z` drafts stay bot-bucket findings.
- `docs/ci.md` + `daily-publish.yml` sweep-job comment: document the artefact-cache lifecycle.

### Test Coverage
- `test/release_artifact_draft_lifecycle_test.dart` — 9 new tests (TDD, written first, RED before the fix): cycle-end reclaim (fresh `ai-gh-*` + `ai-pr-*`), sweep-issue auto-close on cache-only traffic, keep-when-open, 24h backstop for open/unknown state, fail-safe keep on lookup failure, E1 for human `ai-*`, machine `vX.Y.Z` stays a finding, mixed-traffic issue separation — all PASS.
- Regression: `release_hygiene_test.dart` + `release_stale_draft_reclaim_test.dart` + `release_flow_race_test.dart` — 134 tests PASS (gh-2287/gh-2318/gh-2105 semantics preserved).

### Notes
- Sweep-token impact: one extra `GET repos/<repo>/issues/<n>` per cache draft (~5–10/day) — covered by the job's existing `issues: write` grant.
- Cache-loss window is unchanged in practice: closed tickets could already have their cache swept at 24h; a reopened ticket now starts with a fresh session (the restore path is contractually non-fatal).
- The recurring sweep issue this ticket auto-files will close itself on the first post-merge clean sweep.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --

art_swept_tags=""

while IFS=$'\t' read -r bucket tag id created author stale marker_run; do

      # storage). The tag shape was validated by the jq bucket rule, so
      # `gh #<num>` / `pr #<num>` parsing below is total. State lookup:
      # the issues REST API serves PRs too (state=closed covers merged).
      # Any lookup failure yields an empty state — fail-safe: no early
      # reclaim, only the 24h backstop below may delete.
      rest="${tag#ai-}"
      kind="${rest%%-*}"
      num="${rest##*-}"
      state=$(gh api "repos/$repo/issues/$num" 2>/dev/null \
        | jq -r '.state // ""' 2>/dev/null || echo "")

        art_reclaimed_count=$((art_reclaimed_count + 1))
        art_reclaimed="$art_reclaimed- \`$tag\` — created $created by @$author; ticket cycle ended (\`$kind #$num\` closed) — reclaimed at cycle end, no 24h wait: a closed cycle never resumes and the cache is recreated on any future first run (gh-236)\n"

        art_swept_tags="$art_swept_tags $tag"

      # gh-2230 train-draft-guard either ran before the draft existed (a
      # long attach leg created it later) or kept it while its owner was
      # still in-flight. Nothing re-examined such a draft with train
      # knowledge, so it rotted the full 24h and re-filed the recurring
      # sweep issue. Apply the train guard's EXACT criterion here —
      # reclaim only a well-formed-marker draft whose owner run COMPLETED,

      # will ever publish it). Fail-safe keeps mirror the train guard:
